Expand $L=(Xw-y)^T(Xw-y)+\lambda w^Tw$. Its gradient is $2X^T(Xw-y)+2\lambda w$. Setting it to zero gives $(X^TX+\lambda I)\hat w=X^Ty$, hence $\hat w=(X^TX+\lambda I)^{-1}X^Ty$. For $\lambda>0$ the matrix is positive definite even when columns are dependent. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html) [2](https://www.statlearning.com/)

In code solve the linear system, preferably with an appropriate factorization, rather than explicitly forming an inverse. An unpenalized intercept can be handled by centering or excluding its coefficient from the penalty. Standardize features if a common penalty should act comparably across units. If the data-fit term is averaged over samples, the numerical relationship between its lambda and this summed-loss lambda changes by a factor of sample count.
